items.front: Early Vedic (Rigvedic) period dates and chief source?
items.back: c. 1500–1000 BCE; the Rigveda (oldest Veda, Vedic Sanskrit) is the main source.

items.front: Who first called the Aryans a distinct race, and when did they migrate?
items.back: Max Müller; Indo-Iranian speakers migrated c. 1500 BCE via NW passes into the Sapta-Sindhu.

items.front: Aryan-homeland theories: Central Asia / S. Russia / Arctic?
items.back: Central Asia — Max Müller; Southern Russia — Nehring, Gordon Childe; Arctic — B.G. Tilak.

items.front: Non-Indian sources naming Vedic gods, and where found?
items.back: Avesta (Iran); Mitanni inscriptions (Syria — Indra, Varuna, Mitra); Kassite inscriptions (Iraq).

items.front: Sapta-Sindhu — meaning and its seven rivers?
items.back: 'Land of seven rivers': Indus, Saraswati + Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej.

items.front: Rigvedic tribal hierarchy from smallest to largest, with heads?

items.back: Battle of Ten Kings, Rigveda 7th Mandala, on the Parusni (Ravi); Sudas of the Bharatas won → Kuru polity.

items.front: Which Rigvedic assembly elected the Rajan and was headed by him?
items.back: The Samiti (broad clan assembly). The Sabha was a council of elders/noblemen.

items.front: Purushasukta — which Mandala, and what does it establish?
items.back: Rigveda 10th Mandala; names the four Varnas (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra) — start of stratification.
Apala, Lopamudra, Ghosha, Vishwavara — women enjoyed a relatively respected position.

items.front: Rigvedic economy type and chief crops?
items.back: Primarily pastoral (cattle prized); limited agriculture — barley (yava) & wheat; barter, little external trade.

items.front: Most important Rigvedic deity, and Varuna's epithet?
items.back: Indra (thunder/rain/war) most important; Varuna = Ritashya Gopa (guardian of cosmic order). Soma in 9th Mandala.

items.front: Sindhu's epithet, and how often is the Ganga named in the Rigveda?
items.back: Sindhu = Naditama (most sacred, most mentioned); Ganga mentioned only once. ~42 rivers named.
